items.reason: Same two agents; only the moiety spelling differs. Manual §3 requires INN spelling (C5, W2), and the INN for methimazole (registered as "Methimazole (other names: Tapazole)") is thiamazole.

items.coder_A: experimental_combination (uncertain: in Category 1 liothyronine is given only to correct high TSH, could be supportive)
items.reason: Liothyronine is part of the investigational strategy: in Categories 2 and 3 patients "receive liothyronine PO BID to maintain lower free T4 below lower limit of normal", and the summary says giving "methimazole and liothyronine" "could benefit cancer treatment"; it is not symptom control (rule 2), so it is one of two investigational agents (rule 5). Agreed coding stands.

The single arm gives "methimazole, lomustine, liothyronine"; with two investigational agents each is a partner of the other, and lomustine is the backbone. Take B's list with the INN thiamazole. Does not change regimen (combination either way).
